record.title: China issues multi-agency finance guideline for three science and technology hubs
record.summary: A guideline dated 19 October and published by China's Ministry of Science and Technology the next day was jointly issued by 11 central agencies to support finance for innovation hubs in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. It sets 2030 and 2035 goals and directs central-local science funding, regional venture-capital funds, patient capital, a relending pilot for R&D-intensive private SMEs, cross-region finance and data coordination, technology-transfer finance, bond support and selected cross-border services. Regional authorities are asked to prepare implementation rules. The document establishes policy directions, not committed amounts, implementation, capital uptake or economic outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: An official Ministry of Science and Technology page dated 20 October reproduces a 19 October guideline jointly issued by 11 central agencies for financial support to the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta and Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area international science and technology innovation centers.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The guideline sets 2030 goals for a more complete full-chain finance system and increased direct financing, and 2035 goals for a science-finance system adapted to globally influential innovation centers. It directs central-local co-funding for major science tasks, regional venture-capital subfunds, patient capital and a pilot to include R&D-intensive private small and medium enterprises in science-and-technology relending support.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The text calls for cross-region financial-service coordination and information sharing, financing support for technology transfer and commercialization, improved bond financing and credit-risk support, and selected cross-border finance and settlement facilitation. It assigns Beijing, Shanghai and Guangdong authorities to prepare regional implementation rules.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The guideline states policy targets and directions; this source provides no allocated funding totals, detailed eligibility or launch date for the relending pilot, realized capital flows, program uptake or measured innovation outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The guideline assigns regional authorities to prepare implementation rules but the inspected page gives no publication date, exact content, eligibility, instrument budget or operating conditions.
No financing allocation, drawdown, recipient count or private-capital mobilization measure is reported, so the scale and uptake of the announced support are unknown.
The guideline states long-horizon policy goals but presents no evaluated effect on research, commercialization, firm productivity or regional coordination.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, a joint national framework directing public and private financial channels toward science, technology transfer, strategic industries and three major innovation regions could materially alter capital access and interregional innovation finance. The document sets targets and mechanisms but reports no allocation, realized financing, uptake or outcomes; importance reflects potential consequence, not evidence that implementation has occurred.
limitations: The source is an official policy document and establishes what the agencies announced, not subsequent implementation or effects.
It gives no aggregate budget or committed capital amount and no realized financing or uptake data.
The private-SME relending pilot lacks detailed eligibility and launch information in the inspected text; regional implementation rules are assigned for later preparation.
The 2030 and 2035 targets are policy goals, not forecasts or measured results.

technical.claimed_result: The agencies state that coordinated financial measures will strengthen financial support for science and technology in three innovation regions; the document provides targets and instruments but no measured result.

technical.mechanism: The proposed package combines public and private capital: central-local co-funding, regional venture-capital funds and patient capital, a relending pilot for R&D-intensive private SMEs, cross-region finance and information sharing, technology-transfer services, bond guarantees and selected cross-border financing facilitation.
technical.regime: National policy for the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta and Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area innovation centers. The guideline is dated 19 October 2026 and was published by MOST on 20 October; it sets 2030 and 2035 goals and asks regional authorities to prepare implementation rules.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable. This is a policy document without a measured comparison or pre/post outcome analysis.

brief.title: China issues multi-agency finance guideline for three science and technology hubs
brief.why_it_matters: The guideline connects public research funding, patient capital, private-SME credit, technology transfer and cross-border finance across three major Chinese innovation regions. If operationalized, it could change financing pathways for research and technology firms; the text itself does not show what capital will flow or whether the measures will be used.

related.summary: Reported regional follow-through to the Oct 19 multi-agency central guideline, which directed regions to prepare implementation details; this record is a distinct region-specific plan release.

other.title: Reports describe a Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei science-finance implementation plan
other.summary: Two reports dated Oct 21 state that Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei financial and science authorities released a regional implementation plan at the Oct 20 Financial Street Forum. They describe a six-part, 15-measure package spanning long-term capital, research and technology-transfer loans, cross-region financial services, technology insurance and cross-border finance. This development records the reported policy announcement on Oct 21; the signed plan was not recovered, and the reports provide no funding allocation, uptake or outcome evidence.

other.title: China sets out a central policy to link scientific research with industrial innovation
other.summary: A joint Central Committee General Office and State Council opinion published by China’s Ministry of Science and Technology calls for closer integration of scientific research and industrial development. It directs stronger enterprise roles in national science programs and commercialization, a pilot opening of National Natural Science Foundation programs to private firms, greater access for companies to major research infrastructure, instruments and national scientific-data centers, stronger R&D incentives for technology SMEs, and “AI+” deployment across industries. The opinion also identifies embodied intelligence among future-industry fields. The document states policy directions; it gives no funding amounts, named program calls, implementation results or measured effects.
